title: Salman Agha Century Breaks Pakistan Record, Joins Dhoni and Yuvraj List
excerpt: Agha's 107 off 90 balls against Sri Lanka was his fourth ODI hundred batting at No. 5 or lower — passing Mohammad Yousuf's Pakistan record — as Pakistan won the tri-series opener by 37 runs.
body:
• Salman Ali Agha scored 107 off 90 balls as Pakistan made 305 in 49.5 overs and beat Sri Lanka, who were bowled out for 268 in 48.1 overs, by 37 runs in the tri-series opener at Rawalpindi on October 18.
  • It was Agha's fourth ODI century, all of them batting at No. 5 or lower — a new Pakistan record, passing Mohammad Yousuf's three.
  • On the all-time list for hundreds at No. 5 or lower, Jos Buttler and David Miller lead with eight each, followed by MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh with seven each.
  • The century completed a comeback for Agha, who had been removed as T20I captain and dropped from the Test side before rebuilding his form in domestic cricket.

Salman Ali Agha struck 107 off 90 balls to power Pakistan to a 37-run win over Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday, October 18, according to CricTracker. The innings, containing 10 fours and a six, lifted Pakistan to 305 in 49.5 overs and set up a winning start to a tournament that also includes England.

How the Match Turned

Sri Lanka won the toss and chose to bowl, and the decision looked sound while Pakistan's top order struggled. Babar Azam made 45 off 57 balls and Saad Baig added 39, but Pakistan were four wickets down with the innings in danger of stalling when Agha took control at No. 5. He shared a 97-run fifth-wicket stand with Hasan Nawaz, who made 37, reached his century off 82 balls, and was eventually caught by Dasun Shanaka off Asitha Fernando with Pakistan on course for a total above 300.

For Sri Lanka, Eshan Malinga took 4 for 46 and Fernando finished with three wickets. In the chase, Sri Lanka slipped to 91 for 4 before Pavan Rathnayake, with 79, and Janith Liyanage, with 60, revived the innings with a 119-run partnership. With five wickets in hand, Sri Lanka needed 58 runs from the final eight overs, according to Cricket Times, but Pakistan's bowlers triggered a late collapse. Shaheen Afridi took 3 for 55 and Naseem Shah two wickets as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 268 in 48.1 overs.

The Record: Past Yousuf, Chasing Dhoni and Yuvraj

The century was Agha's fourth in 54 ODI appearances, and all four have come batting at No. 5 or lower. That moves him clear of Mohammad Yousuf, who scored three such centuries across a career from 1998 to 2009, as Pakistan's most prolific lower-order centurion in the format. Three of Agha's four hundreds have come specifically at No. 5, a mark he has reached in just 33 matches in that position — he is the first Pakistani batter to score three ODI hundreds at No. 5.

The global list underlines the company he is now keeping. England's Jos Buttler and South Africa's David Miller lead with eight centuries each at No. 5 or lower, India's MS Dhoni and Yuvraj Singh finished with seven each, and AB de Villiers, Andrew Symonds, Eoin Morgan and Sikandar Raza have six each. Agha, at 32, has time to climb further if Pakistan keep him settled in the middle order.

A Comeback Built in Domestic Cricket

The innings carried extra weight because of what preceded it. Agha had been removed as Pakistan's T20I captain, dropped from the Test side and sent home midway through the England tour, and he had not played international cricket since August, according to reports of the match in SportsTak and NDTV's syndicated report. He returned to domestic cricket, scored heavily — including an unbeaten triple century — and forced his way back.

"I don't have enough time to message someone or prove someone wrong. I love my cricket, I love batting and I like playing for Pakistan."

— Salman Ali Agha

After the match, Agha argued that domestic performances are too easily dismissed when senior players drop down to rebuild their game. "I feel that we don't give enough respect to our domestic cricket," he said, pointing to the runs scored by players such as Saud Shakeel and Saad Baig on the same circuit.

What Comes Next

Pakistan face England next in the tri-series at the same venue on October 20. For a side building toward a busy ODI schedule, the value of this win goes beyond the points: Pakistan have found a middle-order batter in form who can both anchor an innings and accelerate, and whose record at No. 5 now stands above any Pakistani before him.
